newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds recoup losses in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds recoup losses in light trade.

text.p: Irish bonds were marginally up on Wednesday, recouping some of Tuesday's losses, with volumes light and largely on the buy side, dealers said.
"We're seeing mostly buying today, as the 10-year bond looks cheap on the curve," a dealer said. "Other than that we're pretty much in line with other European markets, that is, generally lower."
Some dealers noted moderate foreign buying in the afternoon following mostly domestic interest earlier in the session.
"The 10-year bond will probably close about ten pence down on its opening price," a dealer said.
Dealers said U.S. February CPI figures showing a rise of 0.3 percent, compared with forecasts of 0.2 percent, had added to market gloom about the likelihood of an interest rate rise in the U.S.
This was compounding continuing worries about a delay in the timetable for EMU, and speculation in the run-up to the UK general election on May 1.
However, the fundamentals underlying the Irish market remained solid, dealers said.
Attention was focused ahead to Thursday's release of Irish CPI data, dealers said, predicting a year-on-year rise of two percent.
"This is the first year-on-year figure we'll have had for a while but people will probably wait for another few months to see the lie of the land before making any radical moves," a dealer said.

By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up four pence from Tuesday's close to 100.89 to yield 6.26 percent while the benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 12 pence from the close at 107.12 to yield 6.91 percent.
